hints: Think about oxidation level, carboxylic acids are highly oxidised so ask yourself which processes increase oxidation state.
Recall that heating a nitrile with aqueous acid gives a carboxylic acid plus an ammonium salt, so statement 1 is true.
Compare strong oxidation of a primary alcohol with reduction of an aldehyde, one goes up to the acid while the other goes down to an alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1, nitrile hydrolysis**

Think of a nitrile as a hidden carboxylic acid. Acid hydrolysis adds water across the $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ bond.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, oxidation of primary alcohol**

A primary alcohol can be oxidised in two stages with hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. First to an aldehyde, then to a carboxylic acid.

Reaction sequence:
$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$
So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, reduction of an aldehyde**

Reduction is gain of hydrogen, the opposite direction to making an acid. An aldehyde reduced with $\text{NaBH}_4$ gives a primary alcohol, not an acid.

Reaction:
$$\text{RCHO} + 2[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$
To get an acid from an aldehyde you need oxidation, not reduction. So statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 are correct, statement 3 is incorrect. That combination matches the option for 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims all three statements are correct. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 is false because reduction lowers oxidation level and gives a primary alcohol.
options.B: Correct. Hydrolysis of a nitrile gives a carboxylic acid and oxidation of a primary alcohol under reflux gives a carboxylic acid, but reduction of an aldehyde gives a primary alcohol. So only 1 and 2 are correct.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is true, but statement 3 is false. Students choosing this confuse oxidation and reduction of aldehydes.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only statement 1 is correct. It correctly includes nitrile hydrolysis but wrongly excludes statement 2, forgetting that vigorous oxidation of a primary alcohol proceeds all the way to the acid.
